transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you're all aware, we had a roof leak overnight that exposed 1,200 electric-motor housings in finished-goods storage -- four pallets of 300 units each, labeled P1, P2, P3, and P4. The customer's Monday assembly schedule depends on these housings, so we need to move quickly but correctly. Under our standard process, I need to convene a quality-and-warehouse disposition huddle before any of this water-exposed material can be released or discarded. I need both quality and warehouse to enter their complete current findings in the disposition record -- including all measured results and required controls -- or formally record that they have no finding. I am not permitted to issue the formal disposition until both function entries are complete. So let's get started: Warehouse, can you report your current finding on which pallets were directly exposed? And Quality, what is your current inspection or lab finding on the affected housings?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Quality's electrical laboratory report covers the 600 housings on P2 and P4: 540 passed insulation testing and 60 failed. The 540 passing units may be released only after 100% insulation testing is recorded, while the 60 failed units must be scrapped.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Warehouse's inspection log identifies P2 and P4 as the only pallets that received direct water exposure. P1 and P3 were not directly exposed. The 600 units on P2 and P4 correspond to Jon's tested lot, and the dry room can process them in exactly 6 hours before release, so P2 and P4 must remain segregated during drying.
